name: Strawberry
harvest: 12–20 weeks from established plants; seasonal thereafter
climate: Cool to temperate; subtropical varieties available
tip: Keep the crown above soil and mulch under fruit to reduce rot and soil splash.

name: Blueberry
climate: Cool to subtropical depending on cultivar
tip: Grow in acidic soil around pH 4.5–5.5 and choose a cultivar with suitable chill requirements.

name: Raspberry
harvest: Fruit from established canes, commonly second season
climate: Cool to temperate
tip: Trellis canes and prune according to whether the cultivar fruits on first- or second-year canes.

name: Blackberry
climate: Cool to temperate; cultivar dependent
tip: Use cultivated non-invasive varieties and keep canes trained and pruned.

name: Apple
depth: Plant at nursery level with graft above soil
water: Regular while establishing and during fruit swell
climate: Cool to temperate; low-chill cultivars suit warmer districts
tip: Choose a cultivar with the right winter-chill requirement and compatible pollination where needed.

name: Pear
depth: Plant at nursery level with graft above soil
climate: Cool to temperate; chill requirement varies
tip: Many pears crop best with a compatible pollinating cultivar nearby.

name: Peach
climate: Temperate; low-chill cultivars available for warmer regions
tip: Prune annually to maintain productive young wood and good airflow.

name: Nectarine
climate: Temperate; cultivar chill needs vary
tip: Thin crowded young fruit to improve final fruit size and reduce branch stress.

name: Plum
water: Regular while establishing and during fruit swell
climate: Temperate; Japanese and European types differ in chill needs
tip: Check pollination compatibility because some cultivars require another plum nearby.

name: Apricot
climate: Temperate with winter chill and relatively dry ripening weather
tip: Good airflow and a sheltered site help protect blossom and fruit from disease and weather damage.

name: Cherry
climate: Cool to temperate with adequate winter chill
tip: Choose self-fertile cultivars or provide a compatible pollinator; protect ripening fruit from birds.

name: Fig
water: Moderate; regular during establishment and fruiting
climate: Temperate, Mediterranean and subtropical
tip: Avoid excessive nitrogen and provide good drainage; containers can help control vigorous roots.

name: Grape
water: Regular while establishing; moderate once mature
climate: Temperate to warm dry regions depending on cultivar
tip: Provide a strong trellis and prune annually because fruit is produced on new season growth from retained wood.

name: Lemon
depth: Plant at nursery level with graft above soil
climate: Temperate to subtropical; protect young trees from severe frost
tip: Feed with citrus fertiliser during active growth and keep mulch away from the trunk.

name: Lime
climate: Warm temperate to tropical depending on type
tip: Protect frost-sensitive lime varieties in cooler districts.

name: Orange
climate: Temperate to subtropical
tip: Maintain even moisture while fruit develops and avoid burying the graft union.

name: Mandarin
climate: Temperate to subtropical
tip: Thin overcrowded branches rather than heavily pruning productive citrus.

name: Grapefruit
climate: Warm temperate to subtropical
tip: Fruit quality improves with a long warm growing season and consistent moisture.

name: Passionfruit
climate: Warm temperate to tropical depending on cultivar
tip: Provide a strong trellis, mulch the shallow roots and avoid digging around the base.

name: Avocado
depth: Plant slightly high with root flare visible
water: Regular deep watering with excellent drainage
climate: Warm temperate to tropical depending on avocado race/cultivar
tip: Avocados are very sensitive to waterlogged soil; mound planting can help on heavy ground.

name: Mango
water: Regular while young; moderate once established
climate: Tropical to subtropical and warm frost-free sites
tip: Protect young trees from frost and avoid heavy watering during flowering where disease pressure is high.

name: Banana
climate: Tropical to subtropical; warm sheltered sites
tip: Maintain one fruiting stem, one follower and one young sucker for manageable clump production.

name: Pineapple
harvest: 18–24 months, faster from strong slips in warm climates
climate: Subtropical to tropical and warm frost-free sites
tip: Excellent drainage and warmth are essential; avoid burying the central growing point.

name: Rockmelon
water: Regular during growth; reduce as fruit approaches ripeness
climate: Warm-season; frost sensitive
tip: Keep foliage dry where possible and give vines plenty of airflow.

name: Kiwi Fruit
climate: Cool to temperate; chill needs vary
tip: Most cultivars require separate male and female vines, though self-fertile types exist; provide a very strong support.

name: Sunflower
climate: Warm-season across most Australian regions
tip: Tall varieties may need wind protection or staking and are best direct sown.

name: Marigold
climate: Warm-season; long flowering in mild climates
tip: Deadhead regularly to encourage continuous flowers.

name: Nasturtium
climate: Cool to mild; often grown in cooler seasons in hot regions
tip: Avoid rich high-nitrogen soil, which produces leaves at the expense of flowers.

name: Zinnia
climate: Warm-season; frost sensitive
tip: Provide airflow and avoid overhead watering to reduce mildew.

name: Cosmos
climate: Warm-season; adaptable
tip: Do not overfertilise; leaner soil often produces more flowers and less leafy growth.

name: Sweet Pea
sun: Full sun; afternoon shade in warm districts
climate: Cool-season
tip: Provide a trellis and sow early enough to flower before hot weather; ornamental sweet-pea seeds and pods are not edible.

name: Lavender
harvest: Flowers from established plants, often first or second year
climate: Temperate/Mediterranean; select humidity-tolerant types in warmer regions
tip: Excellent drainage and airflow are essential; avoid constantly wet roots.

name: Calendula
climate: Cool to mild
tip: Deadhead frequently for a longer flowering season and allow a few heads to mature if saving seed.

name: Dahlia
depth: Tubers 10–15 cm with shoots near surface
climate: Temperate to subtropical with seasonal management
tip: Stake tall varieties early and avoid heavy watering before tubers have active shoots.

name: Pansy
sun: Full sun in cool weather to part shade
climate: Cool-season
tip: Remove spent flowers and provide afternoon shade as temperatures rise.

name: Warrigal Greens
climate: Temperate to subtropical; tolerates coastal conditions
tip: Blanch leaves before eating and discard the blanching water to reduce oxalates.

name: Lemon Myrtle
water: Regular while young; moderate once established
climate: Subtropical eastern Australia; sheltered warm-temperate sites
tip: Tip-prune to keep the tree compact and produce fresh aromatic foliage.

name: Finger Lime
depth: Plant at nursery level with graft above soil
water: Regular deep watering with good drainage
climate: Subtropical to warm temperate; protect young plants from hard frost
tip: Handle thorny growth carefully and protect young trees from hot drying winds.

name: Davidson Plum
depth: Seed 1–2 cm; plant at nursery level
harvest: 3–5 years depending on species and propagation
sun: Part shade to filtered sun when young
climate: Subtropical to tropical eastern Australia depending on species
tip: Provide shelter and moisture during establishment; fruit is very tart and commonly processed rather than eaten plain.

name: Macadamia
water: Regular while establishing and during nut development
climate: Subtropical to tropical and warm frost-protected sites
tip: Use grafted cultivars for predictable nut quality and protect young trees from wind.
